Karthik / Team —

Finance has reviewed the numbers. We can accommodate upfront recognition of the cash, but two conditions:
1) We need a clear, auditable schedule for the ramp and usage attribution between deliverables vs consumption to satisfy ASC 606 for recognition. The legal team should include explicit amortization language in the SOW.
2) The 55% Year 1 effective discount materially compresses gross margin below our target for this tier. If commercial wants to approve it, we need an offset: either a smaller Year 1 absolute dollar discount (e.g., 45% effective), or a performance-based true-up tied to usage (rebate clawback if usage undershoots).

If we pursue the 55% ask we should:
- Limit the one-off to AtlasHealth only and classify it as a non-recurring concession for recordkeeping.
- Add a step-up clause that restores pricing if they exceed committed usage (protects upside).

I can sign off conditionally if Marketing/Revenue agree to the above controls.

All —

Thanks for the clear asks. I approve a modified concession for AtlasHealth with the following guardrails:

1) Year 1 effective discount capped at 45% (not 55%).
2) Confirmed FY1 prepay allowed at $1.6M given their launch evidence; Finance to document amortization and add a revenue recognition schedule in the SOW.
3) Add a usage true-up clause: if actual consumption in Year 1 is less than 80% of the committed units, we reserve the right to claw back a portion of the concession via a credit applied to Year 2 invoice.
4) Legal to include non-recurring concession language so this doesn't set a precedent for other deals.

Karthik / Vanessa: you can communicate this approval to AtlasHealth and route the final SOW to Legal & Contracts for redlines. If they push back hard on 55% we will not be able to accommodate — this is the maximum concession for this band.
